title: Lexical precision: claim × assert × allege × contend — use

frames.title: Lesson 37 · Lexical precision: claim × assert × allege × contend — use

body: **Foco:** claim × assert × allege × contend — uso.
**Pronúncia:** Ajuste refinado de entonação.
**24 palavras novas** (linguagem especializada).
**Texto do dia:** entrevista.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo escolher claim, assert, allege ou contend para atribuir afirmações num texto jornalístico e justificar a escolha, numa entrevista.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.intro: A legal journalist explains how she attributes statements.
qa: Interviewer: Why does the verb matter so much?

Because it tells readers **how far I vouch** for a statement. If I write that the council **claims** costs fell, I am not endorsing it; if I write that it **asserts** it, I am reporting a confident statement.
**Allege** is for accusations **not yet proved**, usually of wrongdoing. “Prosecutors **allege** theft” is accurate; “prosecutors **claim** theft” sounds oddly casual.
It signals **an argued position** against opposition: “The defence **contends** that the search was unlawful.” It implies **reasoning**, not just assertion.

items.q: Writing “claims” means the journalist endorses the statement.

blocks.body: Perguntas-guia: (1) **está provado?** (2) **o autor endossa?** (3) **há oposição?** Responda e escolha: *claim / assert / allege / contend*.
*Claim* sem *to* ou *that* costuma indicar dúvida; *state* e *say* são neutros.

items.s: The defence ___ that the search was unlawful. (contend)
The minister ___ that the figures were correct. (assert, past)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: Better allege It is not proved

body: **Stand by a statement.** — Sustentar uma declaração.
**Make a bold claim.** — Fazer afirmação ousada.
**Lay the blame on.** — Atribuir a culpa a.
**Plead one’s case.** — Defender seu caso.
**Back up an accusation.** — Embasar uma acusação.
**Deny the charge.** — Negar a acusação.
**Let the facts speak.** — Deixar os fatos falarem.
**Hold up in court.** — Sustentar-se em juízo.
**Innocent until proven guilty.** — Inocente até prova em contrário.
**Testify to.** — Atestar.
**Should I write “prosecutors claim theft”?** — Devo escrever “prosecutors claim theft”?
**Better “allege”. It is not proved.** — Melhor “allege”. Não está provado.
**And for the defence?** — E para a defesa?

forms: Advogados sustentam que as leis se aplicam.

items.label: Ajuste refinado de entonação
items.note: Ajuste refinado de entonação: pequenas variações de altura e de ritmo mudam a atitude (cortesia, ironia, reserva, compromisso) sem mudar as palavras.
words: I suppose that’s one way to put it. ↘↗ (reserva)
Well, that’s ONE way to put it. ↘ (ironia)

prompts.q: Choose the verb: argued legal position.
prompts.model: The defence contends the search was unlawful.
Assert is firm; claim does not endorse.

blocks.task: Write 5 news sentences, each with a different attribution verb and a justification in brackets.
blocks.model: Prosecutors allege that the funds were misused (not yet proved). The defence contends that the audit was flawed (argued position). The minister asserted that the process was lawful (firm statement). The firm claims it acted in good faith (not endorsed). The court heard that the accounts were incomplete.
